notes: $400M draw under the Ayar Third Investment Company (PIF affiliate) Delayed Draw Term Loan (DDTL) facility, drawn 2026-10-06 per Lucid's Form 8-K (filed ~2026-10-09). Outstanding principal under the DDTL is ~$2.1B of a $2.5B facility after this draw, ~$400M capacity remaining. This is a separate tranche from the $800M follow_on already on file for Saudi PIF -> Lucid Group (disclosed 2026-07-06, event id 99) -- not a duplicate of that row, just the same multi-draw facility's next installment.

Conditional loan commitment of up to $5B from DOE's Office of Energy Dominance Financing (UPRISE initiative) for nuclear uprates/modernization across 8 Constellation plants (Braidwood, Byron, Clinton, Dresden, LaSalle, Quad Cities in IL; Calvert Cliffs in MD; Limerick in PA), ~1.1GW total added capacity. NOT yet finalized -- subject to due diligence and definitive financing documents, per both DOE and Constellation releases. Constellation's own PR (constellationenergy.com, 2026-10-27) says most of the added capacity is pre-sold under 20-yr PPAs to Google and Amazon (~$7B of private investment, ~1,080MW) plus a smaller Meta deal (30MW at Clinton) -- these are offtakers, not co-investors; DOE's own release does not name them.

DOE Office of Energy Dominance Financing CLOSED (executed) 30-yr loan package to two Alliant Energy subsidiaries -- Interstate Power & Light (Iowa, up to $3.5B) and Wisconsin Power & Light (Wisconsin, up to $1.626B) -- loan agreements executed 2026-10-26, DOE announced the close 2026-10-28. Funds ~1.6GW new gas-fired generation, 240MW of uprates at existing gas units, ~1GW battery storage, and 2 Bcf of LNG storage (DOE says >2.6GW new/upgraded capacity total). Originally proposed under the Biden administration (Jan 2025) as a $3B conditional commitment; now closed at $5.1B, the Trump administration's 10th financial close under the Energy Dominance Financing Program. Caveat: unlike the Constellation loan this week, neither DOE's nor Alliant's release explicitly ties this capacity to AI/data-center demand -- coverage (e.g. Wisconsin Watch) links regional load growth partly to data centers, but tag as tentative.
